okr.objective: Craebhnat is an Irish heroine honored by a sacred ash tree in Munster.
key_results: Near Doneraile in the southwestern province of Munster, people dedicated a sacred tree to Craebhnat.
When pressed to marry, Craebhnat tore out one of her eyes to drive away her suitor.
A nearby tree kept people afloat, so anyone with a shaving of its bark or wood could never drown.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

text: Craebhnat, also known as Creevna, is an Irish heroine. Near Doneraile, in Munster in the southwest, a sacred ash once honoured her. Pressed to marry, she tore out one of her own eyes. By disfiguring herself she hoped to frighten off the suitor. The ash counted among Ireland's magical trees. A neighbouring tree, so people said, could keep a person afloat. Whoever carried even a chip of its bark or wood would never sink. Whether locals ranked Craebhnat among the fairies or among the saints stays unclear.
